item.title: ERC Advanced Grant Recipients (2016–2024)
item.description:
The ERC Advanced Grant supports established research leaders. The ERC expects an active researcher with a track record of significant research achievements. There is no PhD-based eligibility window — the scheme is open to researchers at any career stage, and the test is the strength of the record and the ambition of the proposed work.

This page lists the funded projects for every Advanced Grant call from 2016 through 2024 — the researcher, host institution, country, research domain, and a direct link to the project record on CORDIS. Use the filters to narrow by call year or by domain (Physical Sciences & Engineering, Life Sciences, Social Sciences & Humanities).

item.title: ERC Consolidator Grant Recipients (2016–2025)
item.description:
The ERC Consolidator Grant supports researchers who defended their PhD more than 5 and up to 15 years ago and are consolidating their own independent research team. The eligibility window can be extended for parental leave, long-term illness, national service and similar documented circumstances. It sits between the Starting Grant and the Advanced Grant, and it is where many researchers make the step from promising to established.

This page lists the funded projects for every Consolidator Grant call from 2016 through 2025 — the researcher, host institution, country, research domain, and a direct link to the project record on CORDIS. Use the filters to narrow by call year or by domain (Physical Sciences & Engineering, Life Sciences, Social Sciences & Humanities).

item.title: ERC Starting Grant Recipients (2016–2025)
item.description: The ERC Starting Grant supports researchers who defended their PhD more than 0 and up to 10 years ago and are starting or have recently started their own independent research team. The eligibility window can be extended for parental leave, long-term illness, national service and similar documented circumstances. It is the ERC scheme that attracts the most applicants each year, and the one most early-career researchers in Europe measure themselves against.

item.title: ERC Synergy Grant Recipients (2018–2025)
item.description:
The ERC Synergy Grant funds a group of two to four principal investigators, at any career stage, who jointly address an ambitious research problem that none of them could tackle alone. It is the ERC’s largest single award and its smallest scheme by number of grants — a few dozen a year.

This page lists the funded projects for every Synergy Grant call from 2018 through 2025 — the principal investigators, host institutions, countries, research domain, and a direct link to the project record on CORDIS. Use the filters to narrow by call year or by domain.
